name: Tech Point Gain Rate
description: Research brings more or fewer tech points: 0.1 to 10 times the normal points, as you choose with the Tech Point Gain Rate slider in the patcher window (it reads -10 to 10: 10 is 10 times, -10 a tenth, -2 half, and 1, the middle, the normal game; 1 unless you move it; type it in the box beside the slider too); the rest of a whole point is a chance, so on average it is exact. The Science level, the speed and every research bonus still count. Island events, duplicate collectibles, puzzles' and messages' rewards and cheats are the game's own. Works with 0.1-10x Tech Cost (prices) and the Origins Tech Point Doubler. **Needs no other patch.** Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it, with the slider at 1. **Unverified in play** (checked by emulation of the game's own code). The companion is "VVFP Tech Gain.dll", started by VVFP More Companions.dll, and the slider's number is written beside it in "VVFP Tech Gain.txt"; nothing is written to a save.
behavior_changes: Tech Point Gain Rate: the companion's sites 0x43B313, 0x43B32E, 0x43B34B (see runtime_detours), installed only when the slider is not 1; N is read at start from "VVFP Tech Gain.txt" beside the companion in tenths (0.1 to 10; none is 1).
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes its sites at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes (all of them, or none; an optional site another patch owns is left alone).
At 1x nothing is installed. The game's rand is never drawn more or less often: the companion's chances are its own numbers.
Nothing is written to a save, a villager record or a file; no text is shown.
evidence_status: implemented from exact-build disassembly of the stock executable; the companion's install and its effect emulated on the rendered executable (tests/test_new_sliders.py); runtime/player confirmation pending
